newsitem.title: USA: Futures funds do well in currencies again in June.
newsitem.headline: Futures funds do well in currencies again in June.

text.p: For the third consecutive month, futures fund managers trading the currency markets were the top performers for the month of June, according to fund monitor TASS Management Ltd.

The majority of the top ten managers realized healthy gains from such trading strategies as as going long the British pound and Japanese yen, while shorting the U.S. dollar, deutschemark and Swiss franc, TASS chief executive Nicola Meaden said.

The British pound saw a two month high against the U.S. dollar in June, while the U.S. dollar slid to a three month low gainst the yen and saw a new four year high against the deutchemark during the month.

But many commodity fund managers also found substantial profit opportunities by going long the interest rate markets in both the U.S. and Europe, and the continued bull market for U.S. stocks led many managers to go long stock index contracts during the month.
Shorting gold and grains and going long zinc were also cited as profitable strategies by several fund managers.
"While currencies still represented a large profit center for many managers, financials and commodities also provided good returns," Meaden said.
The TASS Management monthly report follows the performance of 70 futures and currency managers, each with a minimum of $45 million under management.
TASS Management Ltd is a London-based research company which monitors about 1,600 alternative investment managers with about $11 billion in assets under management globally.
The "alternative investment" universe includes hedge funds, CTAs, managed currency managers, emerging market funds and funds of funds.
